findings.reason: Retaining only the latest reply reference can leave an authorized earlier reply pending after a private reply arrives, and where an index is unavailable the draft gives no capacity or privacy evidence for that exact one-reference limit over a bounded choice of witnesses revalidated at send time.

findings.standard: Verify the State, Not Its Symbol
findings.reason: A disconnected holder may send a reply push using a readable but stale unmuted value even though the send-time check is supposed to establish the reader’s current choice.

findings.standard: An Instar Agent Is Always a Multi-Machine Entity
findings.reason: The draft acknowledges a preference save after local persistence alone, so losing that machine before replication can leave every survivor without the reader’s choice, and the draft does not establish the required Pending receipts, repair, or loss accounting.

findings.standard: Attributed Statements Trace to Their Source
findings.reason: The draft makes an attributed “Chief instruction” binding on full-suite verification without giving Chief’s own words or a checked pointer to the logged instruction.
The opening relies on unexplained terms such as “Chief,” “second server card,” and “normal full verification” before explaining what happens to a reader’s chats and notifications today.

fit.reason: The Archived view, unarchive action, and plain-language mute confirmation support operator-surface quality, but the core design governs preference storage, list filtering, and notification delivery while leaving action placement and phone-width usability to the app.
